posts.title: महाकाली
posts.prompt: Use case: illustration-story / mythic epic. Create a respectful, powerful landscape painterly illustration for the Hindi वीर रस poem Mahakali, depicting Goddess Kali confronting the multiplying demon Raktabija. Mahakali is the unmistakable central divine figure: deep indigo-blue skin, long flowing black hair, luminous fierce eyes, traditional gold crown and ornaments, red draped sari with gold border, stylised small skull-bead necklace treated as devotional iconography. Four clearly separated anatomically coherent arms: one holds a curved sword aloft, one holds a ritual khappar bowl, other hands in protective and commanding gestures. Her tongue slightly extended in traditional iconography, dignified and formidable. Behind and below her, a receding sea of dark demonic silhouettes under a stormy crimson and indigo sky suggests an overwhelming army. A few symbolic red sparks swirl into the ritual bowl before touching the ground, alluding to Raktabija's multiplying blood without depicting wounds. Heroic radiant ochre-gold halo and wind, epic intensity and reverence. Hand-painted gouache with subtle aged-paper texture, rich indigo, muted vermilion and warm gold, cinematic but grounded in Indian devotional narrative art; match a literary blog's painterly storybook illustrations rather than a photoreal film poster. Wide landscape approximately 3:2; keep deity, all arms and weapons readable centrally with breathing room. No human author portrait, no photoreal person, no gore, no severed realistic heads, no exposed organs, no nudity, no graphic blood, no text, captions, logos or watermark. Single coherent scene, not a collage.

note: Both images used inside the posts and for sharing. Original prose, poem lines, metadata and URLs retained.
